record.title: DeepInstructor reports experience-grounded alignment gains on bounded idea-evaluation benchmarks
record.summary: The paper proposes DeepInstructor, which retrieves dimension-specific evaluative relations from a graph built from 58,607 ICLR 2024–2025 reviews. On ExpertEval, a set of 147 ideas with expert scores, the authors report that DeepInstructor using ChatGPT-4o as backbone improves mean Hit@1 and Hit@2 agreement over standalone ChatGPT-4o by 24.4% and 29.7%. Their ICLR-derived DeepInstruct set contains 398 ideas and 289 pairs and shows mixed dimension-specific pairwise and level-accuracy changes. These are paper-reported results; the research desk did not reproduce them.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: DeepInstructor builds a structured experience graph from peer-review data and uses dimension-aware retrieval and agentic reasoning to assess research ideas.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On the paper's ExpertEval set of 147 ideas, the authors report mean Hit@1 and Hit@2 improvements of 24.4% and 29.7% over standalone ChatGPT-4o when DeepInstructor uses the same backbone.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reported results do not establish reliable or generalizable evaluation of research ideas across fields, reviewer populations, or consequential decisions.

evidence_gaps.description: The evaluator and reported benchmark results have not been independently reproduced.
Generalization to independent ideas, reviewer populations and fields beyond computer science is unknown.

brief.importance_rationale: If experience-grounded retrieval improves research-idea evaluation, it could help address the evaluation bottleneck in AI-assisted science. The reported comparisons are limited to author-constructed computer-science benchmarks and do not establish reliable review decisions across domains.
limitations: All result estimates are reported by the authors; the research desk did not reproduce the system or verify the benchmark annotations.
ExpertEval has 147 ideas; DeepInstruct has 398 ideas and 289 pairs, with dataset construction involving LLM extraction and grading plus human validation.
The authors report limited overall performance on significance assessment and restrict their experience graph to two years of computer-science open peer reviews.
The findings do not establish cross-domain validity or safe use in consequential review decisions.
brief.summary: The paper proposes DeepInstructor, which retrieves dimension-specific evaluative relations from a graph built from 58,607 ICLR 2024–2025 reviews. On ExpertEval, a set of 147 ideas with expert scores, the authors report that DeepInstructor using ChatGPT-4o as backbone improves mean Hit@1 and Hit@2 agreement over standalone ChatGPT-4o by 24.4% and 29.7%. Their ICLR-derived DeepInstruct set contains 398 ideas and 289 pairs and shows mixed dimension-specific pairwise and level-accuracy changes. These are paper-reported results; the research desk did not reproduce them.

technical.claimed_result: On ExpertEval (147 ideas), DeepInstructor with ChatGPT-4o reports 24.4% higher mean Hit@1 and 29.7% higher mean Hit@2 than standalone ChatGPT-4o. The system also reports results on DeepInstruct (398 ideas, 289 pairs) and an AI-in-the-loop refinement experiment.
technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv v1 paper reports the design, datasets and comparisons. the research desk inspected the paper but did not run the system or independently validate the annotations or results.
technical.mechanism: A graph of evaluative relations extracted from ICLR reviews supports entity- and relation-aware retrieval; a ReAct-style agent generates dimension-specific comments, and a separate prompted scorer maps comments to scores.
technical.regime: Computer-science research-idea evaluation. ExpertEval includes 147 ideas and human scores; DeepInstruct is constructed from ICLR 2026 reviews and includes 398 ideas and 289 pairs. The Experience Graph uses ICLR 2024 and 2025 reviews.
technical.strongest_baseline: Standalone ChatGPT-4o with the same backbone on ExpertEval; additional comparisons include passage-level RAG, DeepReview, ChatGPT-4o-mini and DeepSeek-V4-Pro. The constructed DeepInstruct set shows mixed pairwise and level-accuracy changes across dimensions.

brief.title: DeepInstructor reports experience-grounded alignment gains on bounded idea-evaluation benchmarks
brief.why_it_matters: Research-idea assessment may become a bottleneck as AI systems generate more candidate work. This paper tests whether retrieved reviewer experience can improve score alignment and concern-level evaluation, while its bounded datasets and weak significance-assessment results leave cross-domain validity unresolved.
